_comment: Every command below shares one interpreter probe, `_pyexe`. It RUNS each
candidate before accepting it, rather than trusting the first name that
resolves.
The previous form was `command -v python3 || command -v py || command -v
python`, and on Windows that is actively wrong: `python3` commonly resolves
to the Store alias stub in WindowsApps, which exists and is executable, so
`command -v` SUCCEEDS and the `||` fallbacks never fire. Every dispatched
hook was then invoked through an interpreter that cannot run it — the hook
exited non-zero without producing output, and because a PreToolUse hook
that fails to run is indistinguishable from one that ran and allowed, the
entire guard set silently did nothing. Reproduced by putting a
non-functional `python3` first on PATH: current probe picks it and the hook
exits 9009 with no warning; this probe skips it.
These wirings go FURTHER than the launchers did: they assert the
interpreter's VERSION via stdout, where `claw` settled for a bare
`-c "import sys"` liveness check that passes on Python 2.7 and on any
wrapper that swallows `-c`. This block used to claim `claw` 'already
carried this exact probe' and that 'the hooks now match it' — inverted on
both counts. `claw` has since been raised to the stdout form; `claw.cmd`
reaches a paren-free `assert` instead, because the stdout form needs a
`print(...)` inside a parenthesised `if` block that cmd cannot parse. What
IS pinned across all of them is the candidate ORDER.
Note also that JSON has no substitution: `_pyexe` is a reference copy, and
`test_every_wiring_shares_one_probe` is what holds the inlined copies equal
to it.
Failure is announced rather than silent: if NO candidate runs, the command
says so on stderr and exits 1. NON-ZERO is deliberate, and this block used
to say 'exits 0 (fail-open)' — describing, as intended behaviour, exactly
the invisible degradation the probe exists to prevent. stderr from an
exit-0 hook reaches the debug log only, so a machine with no usable Python
would have looked protected while running no guards at all.
`test_every_wiring_exits_non_zero_when_no_interpreter_works` pins the 1;
the code and the test were fixed once already and this comment was not,
which matters because it is the sentence a future editor consults before
changing that exit code.
_pyexe: PYEXE=; for c in python3 py python; do p=$(command -v $c 2>/dev/null) || continue; [ "$("$p" -c "import sys; print(1 if sys.version_info >= (3,8) else 0)" 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] && PYEXE=$p && break; done; if [ -z "${PYEXE:-}" ]; then echo "cla: no working python interpreter (tried python3, py, python) — guard hooks are NOT running" >&2; exit 1; fi;

hooks.command: PYEXE=; for c in python3 py python; do p=$(command -v $c 2>/dev/null) || continue; [ "$("$p" -c "import sys; print(1 if sys.version_info >= (3,8) else 0)" 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] && PYEXE=$p && break; done; if [ -z "${PYEXE:-}" ]; then echo "cla: no working python interpreter (tried python3, py, python) — guard hooks are NOT running" >&2; exit 1; fi; "$PYEXE" "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/guard-worktree-isolation.py" --heartbeat
